title: Instrumentation workflow hiccup report — 2026-12-03
content:
Observability sync notes (rapid postmortem / weekly capture) — 2026-12-03

Attendees: Priya, Marco, Lina, Evan, Rohan (brief), SRE oncall (Anya)
Location: Zoom + #obs-trace

TL;DR:
- We saw an intermittent increase in tracing span volume during the weekend synthetic run (approx +3.8x baseline for route /api/stream). This exposed a memory pressure bug in trace-agent v1.9 (KV cache growth).
- Short-term mitigations applied: rollback agent to v1.8 on affected clusters, apply 50% sampling for low-tier customer routes, and pause a scheduled synthetic test job.
- Longer-term: implement dynamic sampling by client tier + route weight, add span-heatmap dashboard with drilldown, and add cost-telemetry alerting for synthetic-run anomalies.

Standup-style updates (quick bullets):
- Priya: Rolled back trace-agent v1.9 on 3 clusters (eu-west-1 & us-west-2). Logged evidence in INF-2345. Verified traces stable after rollback. TODO: add automated rollback playbook to release pipeline. (ETA: 2026-12-06)
- Marco: Implemented temporary sampling hook in routing layer; sampling flag honored at gateway to reduce frontloaded KV growth. Observed 40% drop in span ingestion rate for test traffic. Need to propagate sampling headers into traces ingestion path. Action: PR to obs-ingest (PR 712) for header passthrough.
- Lina: Built the first draft of "Span Heatmap by Customer" in Metabase using a materialized BigQuery view. Prototype shows hotspots for top 10 routes. Need UX for drilldowns and customer filtering.
- Evan: Investigated cost telemetry spike and confirmed synthetic job running nightly had wrong concurrency setting (was 200 -> should be 20). Disabled job and filed INF-2399 to enforce job-level quotas.
- Anya (SRE): Oncall handoff notes — no ongoing pager after rollback; heap growth stopped. Suggested adding span-agent-memory as a new metric and an alert at 75% of heap.

Incident timeline (short):
- 2026-12-02 22:10 UTC: Synthetic run kicks off (misconfigured concurrency).
- 2026-12-03 00:40 UTC: Tracing ingestion alert fires (span dropouts + high GC) on cluster eu-west-1.
- 2026-12-03 01:15 UTC: Debug session, identify spike pattern tied to route /api/stream + agent v1.9.
- 2026-12-03 02:00 UTC: Rollback v1.9 -> v1.8 on affected nodes.
- 2026-12-03 03:00 UTC: Observability metrics stabilize.

Technical notes / root-cause hypothesis:
- Agent v1.9 introduces an experimental KV caching path that doesn't bound prefix table entries in certain high-cardinality tagging scenarios. When span rate is high and many unique tags are present, the in-memory map grows without eviction.
- The trace ingest pipeline backpressure was insufficient — ingestion buffers filled and GC pressure spiked which led to span processing lag and partial drop.
- Two orthogonal contributors: (1) synthetic job concurrency misconfig, (2) unbounded cache growth in agent.

Short-term mitigations (what we did):
- Rollback agent to v1.8 on affected clusters (Priya).
- Pause nightly synthetic job and adjust concurrency (Evan).
- Flip on 50% sampling for non-SLO customer tiers on vulnerable routes (Marco).
- Add temporary ingestion throttling rule: cap spans/sec per host for 1 week.

Medium-term work (tracked as tasks):
- RFC: Dynamic sampling policy by customer tier and route weight (owner: Marco). Scope: allow policy to reference recent cost-telemetry signals (e.g., tokens/route) and apply probabilistic sampling with sticky client decisions. Target: reduce tail ingestion spikes without hurting SLO routes. (Linked: INF-2410)
- Fix: Add eviction and soft limits to agent KV cache and add a metrics export for cache-size-by-taggroup (owner: Priya). Unit tests + stress test needed. (ETA proposal: 2 weeks).
- Dashboard: Iterate on Span Heatmap prototype to include per-customer drilldown and a temporal slider (owner: Lina). UX ask: include cost-per-span estimate to prioritize hotspots.
- Alerting: Create cost-telemetry anomaly alert that triggers when synthetic-run cost > 2x median and spans ingestion > 2x baseline for 30m (owner: Evan).

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Do we prefer sampling at gateway vs at agent? Gateway sampling reduces ingest but loses some fidelity for downstream attribution. Agent-side sampling preserves fidelity for local traces but doesn't prevent KV growth. Need a hybrid approach proposal.
- Thresholds: what are safe default sampling levels by customer tier? (proposal: free/demo=10%, startup=25%, standard=50%, enterprise=100% unless SLO flagged)
- Synthetic tests policy: should all heavy synthetic runs require a canary quota reservation? (suggestion: yes, schedule through CI job that requests a quota token)

Notes-to-self / rough TODOs:
- Draft rollback playbook and attach to release checklist (Priya)
- Add agent cache metrics to prom-exporter and create dashboard panel (Priya + Lina)
- Finish PR 712 for header passthrough and get it to staging (Marco)
- Update synthetic job configs and create CI gate for concurrency (Evan)

Meeting artifacts / follow-ups:
- INF-2345 (agent memory growth incident), INF-2399 (synthetic job misconfig), INF-2410 (dynamic sampling RFC)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/712 (sampling header passthrough)
- Design doc: confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Span+Heatmap+Design

Misc notes / random fragments:
- "If we add event-level cost attribution we can show per-customer COGS of tracing — helps product ask for budget."
- Consider marking large synthetic jobs with a request-id header so they get sampled automatically.
- Check whether on-prem private deployments include the same agent; we should coordinate with private-deployments team to avoid the same bug escaping air-gapped installs.

Next sync: quick follow-up 2026-12-06 14:00 PT to review progress on agent fix + sampling RFC.

-- end of notes --
